title: Xanthe and the Ember
premise: Mara Oyelaran, a debt-bound scribe in the Ember Guild's counting house, discovers tonight's date inked in a century-old prophecy ledger — and that night the guild's newest courier, Xanthe, arrives carrying a sealed ember that predates the last great war. The prophecy names a bearer who must either surrender the ember to the temple (reigniting the war) or destroy it (unmaking the guild's magic and Mara's debt with it). As temple inquisitors close in and the guild betrays its own couriers to save itself, Mara and Xanthe learn the prophecy was forged by the guild's founder to manufacture her own legitimacy. In the end, Mara falsifies the one ledger no one dares audit — the prophecy itself — erasing the date, freeing Xanthe, and choosing an unwritten future over both justice and survival.
about_author: Ivo Nakamura is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing merchant guild records in port cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, debt, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet the Ember Guild's counting house: debts paid in memories, favors, years of life. Mara balances books he can never afford to leave. Emotional beat: weary competence masking quiet desperation.

chapters.title: A Date That Hasn't Happened
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Auditing the founder's sealed archive, he finds tonight's exact date written in a century-old prophecy ledger, circled twice. He tells himself it's coincidence. Emotional beat: dread creeping through denial.

chapters.title: The Courier at the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A courier arrives half-dead through the guild's back gate, clutching a lead-sealed case that burns cold. The guildmaster takes the case; Xanthe refuses to let it out of sight. Emotional beat: stubborn loyalty meeting institutional suspicion.

chapters.title: Terms of Debt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The guild assigns Mara to Xanthe as handler — his debt extended if the courier defects. Their first conversation reveals Xanthe doesn't know what he carries. Emotional beat: wary transactional alliance.

chapters.title: What Burns Cold
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe describes how he received the case from a dying woman in the marshes who called it 'the last honest thing.' Mara recognizes the seal mark from the founder's archive. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Summons
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Temple inquisitors arrive demanding inspection of guild ledgers — including the sealed archive. The guildmaster orders Mara to forge a clean copy overnight. Emotional beat: complicity tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Book
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Comparing the forged copy to the original, Mara finds the prophecy text altered between editions — someone rewrote history. He keeps the discrepancy secret even from Xanthe. Emotional beat: the first deliberate lie of his own.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Mercy
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vess's POV. Vess privately burns a courier's contract to protect him, revealing she knows what the ember truly is — and what the founder did. She warns Mara to stop asking questions. Emotional beat: kindness used as a leash.

chapters.title: Night Market of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe drags Mara into the city's underground market to find the dead courier-woman's sister. They learn the ember was stolen FROM the temple — it's the war's original cause, not its cure. Emotional beat: vertigo of a flipped story.

chapters.title: Marked for Audit
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. An inquisitor finds Mara's marginalia in the archive and offers him immunity to testify against the guild. Mara realizes the temple doesn't want truth either — it wants the ember back. Emotional beat: temptation of the lawful betrayal.

chapters.title: The Case Opens
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Cornered by guild enforcers who intend to hand the ember over, Xanthe breaks the seal. Inside: not a weapon but a living flame that shows each viewer their own worst act. It shows Xanthe abandoning the dying woman. Emotional beat: guilt made visible.

chapters.title: What Mara Saw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The flame shows Mara the moment he let his brother take his place in debtor's prison. He confesses everything to Xanthe — the forgery, the altered prophecy, the inquisitor's offer. Emotional beat: catharsis through confession.

chapters.title: The Founder's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Deep in the archive, Mara proves the original prophecy was penned by the guild's founder herself — a manufactured destiny to sanctify the guild's founding theft. The date isn't fate; it's a deadline she set. Emotional beat: fury at a dead architect.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Counting House
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Vess trades Xanthe to the inquisitors to save the guild, and Mara's forged ledgers are exposed as evidence against HIM. Xanthe escapes custody because the flame won't leave his hands. Emotional beat: loyalty repaid with sale.

chapters.title: Fugitives in the Ledger Stacks
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleaved. Hunted through the guild's labyrinthine archive, they hide among records of every debt ever owed — including the founder's own unpaid debt to the temple. Emotional beat: terror becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Unpaid Debt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The founder's oldest entry reveals she promised the flame would be returned 'when the book says so' — meaning the prophecy's date was her escape clause, and destroying the ember voids every guild contract, including Mara's. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as ruin.

chapters.title: Vess at the Door
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess finds them first — not to capture them, but to beg them to run and let the guild survive on the lie. Mara refuses: the couriers she sold deserve the truth. Emotional beat: grief between people who understand each other too well.

chapters.title: The Temple's Empty Heart
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They infiltrate the temple to return the ember publicly, and find the war-god's altar hollow — the temple has been guarding nothing for a century, sustained by the lie alone. Emotional beat: awe curdling into pity.

chapters.title: Ash and Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax, both POVs. Confrontation atop the temple steps: inquisitors, Vess, the guild's enforcers. Xanthe offers the flame to anyone willing to look at their worst act; the inquisitors refuse, and their refusal unmasks them before the crowd. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon that cuts only those who dodge it.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Rather than return or destroy the ember, Mara writes the founder's debt PAID IN FULL in the prophecy ledger and seals it — dissolving the guild's claim, his own debt, and the prophecy's power in a single stroke. The flame gutters out, spent. Emotional beat: terrible liberation.

chapters.title: Audited by No One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Aftermath: the guild collapses into ordinary trade, Vess faces her couriers' families, and the temple must decide what to worship now. Xanthe, free of the case for the first time, chooses to stay in the city. Emotional beat: raw, unglamorous freedom.

chapters.title: A Blank Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara opens a new ledger with no debts in it and writes the first honest entry of his life: his own name, owed to no one. He and Xanthe walk out past the ruined counting house together. Emotional beat: quiet beginning after the price has been paid.
